name: JSW Steel Ltd.
business_summary: India's second-largest steel producer (JSW Group), integrated flat and long products at Vijayanagar, Dolvi, Salem and Bhushan Power & Steel, with captive iron ore in Karnataka/Odisha and a growing downstream (coated, special steels) and export tail. Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026) sales Rs54,486 cr, EBITDA Rs10,120 cr (19%), consolidated PAT Rs5,359 cr (about three-fold YoY; some outlets quote Rs5,279 cr), record volumes. TTM sales Rs199,021 cr, EBITDA Rs34,248 cr; market cap Rs3.32 lakh cr. Board approved Rs7,500 cr Sambalpur expansion on 2026-10-22.

exposures.mechanism: Domestic HRC/long-product price. ~88% of TTM sales Rs199,021 cr is domestic; +7% price on that = ~Rs12,200 cr vs TTM EBITDA Rs34,248 cr (17% margin) => +36% EBITDA at constant cost; EV/MCap ~1.25, persistence 0.3 => +13.5. Cut to 9 because price rises historically coincide with coking-coal cost rises (spread beta < 1) and pass-through lags. Pack empirical on global HRC is small (+1.10 per +10%, t=+2.0).

evidence.note: Reuters: Indian steel prices set to rise further on coking coal costs, demand revival
NDTV Profit: steel prices at import parity
Moneycontrol: profit +225% YoY on record sales, firm flat steel prices

exposures.mechanism: Imported coking coal ~27% of total costs (TTM expenses Rs164,773 cr => ~Rs44k cr; model estimate). +15% => -19.6% EBITDA at constant prices; ~35% passed through within a quarter => -12.7%; x1.25 x0.3 persistence => ~-4.8 to -7; central -5.5. Reuters 2026-08-19 flags a mill margin squeeze on rising coking coal.

evidence.note: Reuters: mills face margin squeeze as global coking coal rises
Argus: China supply shocks and coking coal trends

exposures.mechanism: Net purchased ore ~8% of costs after captive Karnataka/Odisha mines (model estimate); +15% => ~Rs2,000 cr => -5.8% EBITDA, ~50% passed through, x1.25x0.3 => ~-1.1 to -2. Pack empirical is POSITIVE (+2.33, t=+2.3) because ore and steel prices co-move; conflict flagged: cost-side sign retained, steel-price co-movement is captured in F_STEEL_INDIA.

evidence.note: empirical +2.33 per +15% iron ore, t=+2.3 (sign conflict)
ET: NMDC lump Rs5,250/t, fines Rs4,500/t

exposures.mechanism: Import-parity domestic pricing and ~13% exports lift INR revenue ~+2.2% for +3% USD/INR (~Rs4.4k cr); imported coal/ore ~30% of costs (+Rs1.5k cr); USD debt revaluation ~-Rs0.7k cr; net ~+Rs2.2k cr = +6% EBITDA x1.25 x0.3-0.5 => ~+2.5.

evidence.note: Interest Rs1,602 cr in Q2 FY27 vs Rs2,413 cr a year earlier (debt falling)

exposures.mechanism: Interest Rs7.8k cr TTM on net debt of roughly Rs70k cr (model estimate), ~50% floating or short; +25bp = ~Rs90 cr = 0.3% EBITDA; most of the effect is the discount rate on a levered cyclical (beta ~1.1): ~-1.2.

evidence.note: Investing.com: record volumes drive profit surge, debt falls

exposures.mechanism: Infrastructure/construction ~40% of Indian steel demand; +10% government capex lifts industry volumes ~2-3% and supports price; JSW (domestic volumes ~25 Mt run-rate, model knowledge) EBITDA +4% => x1.25x0.5 => ~+2.

evidence.note: ETV Bharat: steel boom has upsides and downsides
PIB: steel demand robust in Apr-Aug 2026

exposures.mechanism: Flat products to autos/white goods/ appliances are ~20-25% of JSW volumes (model knowledge); +10% auto volumes => +1.5% JSW volumes => ~+3% EBITDA x1.25x0.2... => ~+0.8.

Volume-protection effect of safeguard/anti-dumping duties beyond the price channel (price already in F_STEEL_INDIA); SMM 2026-10-07 reports ministry unlikely to tighten curbs, so incremental upside is limited while removal risk is the downside.

evidence.note: Shanghai Metals Market: ministry unlikely to tighten import curbs
Business Standard: EU quota opens 2.8 MT export window for India

exposures.mechanism: Exports (~12% of volume) benefit from a 2.8 Mt EU quota window but CBAM raises landed cost; small net exposure.

evidence.note: Rediff MoneyWiz: India secures 2.8 MT EU steel quota

exposures.mechanism: Steel demand growth ~1.2x GDP; residual after capex and auto edges (kept small to avoid double counting).
